question: We're developing a copper-toned blush and want to use copper powder as the colorant. May we, and what restrictions, certification or labeling apply?
key_elements: Yes. 73.2647(b) lists copper powder for coloring cosmetics generally, including cosmetics intended for use in the area of the eye, in amounts consistent with good manufacturing practice (no numeric cap). It must conform in identity and specifications to § 73.1647(a)(1) and (b) ((a)). The additive and its color mixtures bear § 70.25 labeling ((c)). Batches are exempt from section 721(c) certification ((d)).

73.2647.head: (a) Identity and specifications. The color additive copper powder shall conform in identity and specifications to the requirements of § 73.1647 (a)(1) and (b).
73.2647.tail: powder shall conform in identity and specifications to the requirements of § 73.1647 (a)(1) and (b).

73.2647.tail: ics intended for use in the area of the eye, in amounts consistent with good manufacturing practice.

73.2647.head: (c) Labeling. The color additive and any mixture prepared therefrom intended solely or in part for coloring purposes shall conform to the requirements of § 70.2
